items.title: Optional feature bundle lacks per-capability contracts
items.statement: The omnibus optional-feature sentence lists nine LSP capabilities but does not define callers, capability negotiation, supported/unsupported/loading/empty/error/cancelled states, result limits, or per-feature consumers. Because the unit is also marked split-recommended, treating the list as one implementable contract leaves materially different feature lifecycles unresolved.
items.impact: Implementations can expose controls that have no server capability, silently conflate empty results with failure, or return results to inconsistent Interview/editor surfaces.
items.builder_discretion: Split the capabilities into explicit contracts with caller, consumer, capability-advertisement, state, cancellation, limits, and fallback behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Optional Interview and editor enhancements may include structure-of-file via documentSymbol, diagnostics in interview context, type definition, implementation, document links, call hierarchy, folding range, selection range, and document highlight.
split_recommended: true

items.title: Gate trigger and scope snapshot are not concurrency-safe
items.statement: Tier-boundary execution and changed_files/open/project scope are named, but the contract does not say when the scope is snapshotted, how simultaneous task/subtask/phase boundaries deduplicate, whether overlapping runs serialize, or how edits and diagnostic publications arriving during a run affect the verdict.
items.impact: The same boundary can produce duplicate or contradictory gate results, and a verdict can describe a different file set than the one that was evaluated.
items.builder_discretion: Define boundary identity, scope snapshot time, overlap/deduplication rules, diagnostic-version pinning, and cancellation/restart semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The LSP diagnostics verification gate runs at configured tier boundaries, defaults to phase boundary only, treats iteration-local preflight as advisory only, checks changed_files, open, or project scope, and blocks by configurable error or error_and_warning severity threshold.

items.title: Advisory preflight cannot replace the configured gate
items.statement: The negative constraint explicitly prevents an iteration-local advisory preflight from substituting for the configured tier-boundary gate, closing a common false-success path.

evidence.exact_quote: - Iteration-local preflight MUST NOT replace the configured boundary gate.

items.title: Configuration precedence, validation, and migration are absent
items.statement: The config location and defaults are stated, but the contract does not define project-versus-global precedence, which actor may change a project override, validation of unknown or malformed values, behavior on partial config reads, forward/backward compatibility, or migration of existing configuration.
items.impact: An untrusted or malformed project file can weaken verification, different clients can resolve the same settings differently, and upgrades can silently change gate behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Specify the merge order, trust and write authority, schema/version rules, invalid-value behavior, migration behavior, and auditable provenance of the effective configuration.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The LSP gate config lives at verification.lsp_gate with opt-in defaults, changed_files scope, errors-only blocking, phase boundary, 10-second timeout, skip when unavailable, and project override through .puppet-master/config.json.
- Plans/LSPSupport.md owns LSP-specific protocol/client constraints while referenced owner docs retain their SSOT boundaries.

items.title: Blocking-severity token is internally inconsistent
items.statement: The gate contract preserves error_and_warning while the config-default unit preserves errors_and_warnings. The singular/plural mismatch is not identified as an alias or migration rule, so serialization, validation, and UI round-tripping can disagree.
items.impact: A valid UI choice can serialize to a value rejected or ignored by the verifier, potentially allowing warnings that the user intended to block.
items.builder_discretion: Choose one canonical enum value and define explicit alias rejection or migration for the other token.

items.title: Unavailable LSP silently skips a requested safety gate
items.statement: The default when_unavailable behavior is skip, but no result state distinguishes skipped-unavailable from passed, no user-facing warning is required, and no policy says whether repeated outages, server crashes, initialization delays, or offline remote servers escalate.
items.impact: Work may advance with no diagnostics while the Dashboard or criterion appears successful, defeating the user-selected verification intent.
items.builder_discretion: Define a first-class unavailable/skipped verdict, visible reason and provenance, retry/escalation policy, and whether enabled gates may fail open by authority tier.

items.title: Verification controls lack transactional and truthful GUI states
items.statement: The control list and shared blob binding omit save/apply/cancel semantics, dirty and conflict states, inherited-versus-overridden indication, disabled dependencies, invalid input handling, concurrent external edits, unavailable-server feedback, keyboard/focus/error associations, and localization-safe labels.
items.impact: The GUI can display values different from the effective config, overwrite newer settings, or expose controls that screen-reader and keyboard users cannot reliably interpret.
items.builder_discretion: Define the form state machine, effective-value provenance, validation and conflict UI, accessibility semantics, and localization requirements.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The Verification tab exposes an LSP diagnostics gate subsection with enable, scope, block-on, tier-boundary, and timeout controls bound to the same VerificationConfig blob.

items.title: Failure recovery is delegated without LSP-specific invariants
items.statement: Routing through the standard orchestrator is appropriate, but this unit does not define which failures are retryable, whether retry refreshes or pins scope, how partial diagnostic responses and timeouts map to passed/met, how cancellation is represented, or how evidence and notifications deduplicate across retries.
items.impact: Retries can change the evaluated target, duplicate evidence and toasts, or convert infrastructure failure into a diagnostic failure or success inconsistently.
items.builder_discretion: Define failure taxonomy, retry idempotency key, scope/version rules, partial-result handling, cancellation, and terminal evidence aggregation.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: When LSP diagnostics fail the gate, the criterion result carries passed false, met false, and an actual diagnostic summary, then follows standard orchestrator retry, escalation, or stop policy with no special LSP-only gate-runner path.

items.title: LSP failures use the standard orchestrator path
items.statement: The explicit prohibition on a special LSP gate path prevents a second retry/escalation authority from diverging from standard failed-gate governance.

evidence.exact_quote: - The LSP gate must use the standard failed-gate flow rather than a special-case orchestrator path.

items.title: Failure notification lacks stale, privacy, and accessible-copy rules
items.statement: The notification path does not distinguish current from historical or superseded failures, define dismissal and update behavior, redact file paths and diagnostic text, constrain evidence access, provide accessible announcement/focus behavior, or make dynamic count copy localizable.
items.impact: Users can act on stale failures, sensitive source data can leak through toast/report text, and assistive-technology or non-English users may not receive an intelligible failure state.
items.builder_discretion: Specify freshness and supersession, redaction and authorization, durable versus transient behavior, accessibility announcement semantics, and parameterized localized copy.

items.title: Failure truth has a durable inspection path
items.statement: The standard Dashboard/Gate report path plus attached inspectable evidence prevents the optional toast from being the sole failure record.

items.title: Snapshot evidence has no secure lifecycle or attachment-failure contract
items.statement: Always capturing a diagnostic snapshot does not define atomic write/attach behavior, response to EvidenceStore failure, redaction of source text and paths, authorization, encryption, retention, quota and eviction, deduplication, corruption detection, or authorized deletion and its audit trail.
items.impact: Sensitive diagnostics can persist indefinitely or be exposed, storage can grow without bound, and a gate verdict can claim evidence that was never durably stored.
items.builder_discretion: Define snapshot schema, atomicity and failure policy, access controls, redaction, integrity, retention/quota/eviction, and auditable deletion semantics.

items.title: Evidence capture is symmetric for pass and fail
items.statement: The unit explicitly requires a snapshot for both successful and failed runs, avoiding a success-only evidence blind spot and preserving the basis for later comparison.

items.title: Interdependent gate units declare no dependency graph
items.statement: Config, GUI, failure flow, notification, and evidence units all declare empty dependencies even though the GUI binds the config, gate failure feeds orchestrator and notification, and every run must attach evidence. Callers, consumers, ordering, and cross-document contracts are therefore not machine-visible.
items.impact: Compilation or implementation can schedule consumers before providers, omit required evidence/notification integration, or assign conflicting SSOT ownership.
items.builder_discretion: Declare PlanUnit dependencies and named ContractRefs to the configuration, verifier registry, orchestrator criterion, GateReport, Dashboard, and EvidenceStore owners.

items.title: Acceptance criteria do not falsify runtime or GUI behavior
items.statement: The repeated acceptance criteria establish source preservation and index validation, but provide no executable oracle for trigger timing, effective config, severity filtering, unavailable behavior, retries, GUI persistence, notifications, or evidence durability and privacy.
items.impact: All listed validators can pass while every user-facing and runtime contract in these units remains incorrectly implemented or unimplemented.
items.builder_discretion: Add deterministic contract tests and GUI/state oracles for each unit, including negative, concurrent, unavailable, partial-failure, migration, accessibility, and lifecycle cases.

items.title: Gate results and snapshots lack operational provenance
items.statement: An actual summary and lsp_snapshot reference are required, but neither contract requires run and boundary identity, timestamps, workspace/config/scope digest, LSP server identity/version, diagnostic document versions, retry attempt, duration, timeout/unavailable reason, truncation, or correlation across criterion, report, notification, and evidence.
items.impact: Support cannot reproduce a verdict, distinguish stale from current diagnostics, correlate duplicate runs, or determine whether missing diagnostics were caused by timeout, truncation, or an unavailable server.
items.builder_discretion: Define a versioned result/evidence envelope with stable correlation IDs and the minimum provenance needed for reproduction and support.

items.title: Project scope and fixed timeout lack scale and partial-result semantics
items.statement: Whole-project scope is offered with a fixed 10-second default, but no file/diagnostic/byte ceilings, paging or streaming policy, backpressure, cancellation, cache policy, truncation marker, partial-result verdict, or adaptive timeout behavior is specified.
items.impact: Large repositories can time out nondeterministically, exhaust memory, or pass on an incomplete diagnostic subset without telling the user.
items.builder_discretion: Define bounded collection, cancellation/backpressure, truncation and partial-result truth, and timeout policy per scope with scale-focused acceptance tests.

dimension_assessments.summary: Optional feature consumers are unnamed and the gate units omit their dependency/caller graph.
Unsupported, unavailable, skipped, malformed-config, dirty/conflicted GUI, cancelled, and superseded states are not fully specified.
Boundary deduplication, scope/diagnostic version pinning, overlapping retries, config conflicts, and evidence attachment races are undefined.
Unavailable servers, timeout/truncation, partial diagnostic responses, and evidence-store failures lack verdict semantics.
Config rollback/migration, retry idempotency, cancellation, and recovery from failed evidence persistence are absent.
Project-override write authority and evidence read/delete authority are not defined; owner notes do not name the referenced SSOT contracts.
Diagnostics, paths, summaries, notifications, and snapshots lack redaction, retention, access, quota, eviction, and deletion rules.
Project configuration and LSP-supplied diagnostic/message/path content have no validation, normalization, redaction, size, or rendering-safety contract.
The GUI can conceal skipped-unavailable execution, show non-effective config, or present stale/superseded failures as current.
Unavailable remote servers default to skip without offline/reconnect truth, escalation, or partial-result handling.
Whole-project diagnostics and always-on snapshots have no collection, storage, timeout, truncation, quota, or backpressure limits.
Verification controls and failure announcements lack keyboard, focus, accessible-name/error association, and assistive-technology behavior.
Control labels and dynamic diagnostic-count failure copy lack parameterization, pluralization, expansion, and translation requirements.
Config migration is unspecified and error_and_warning conflicts with errors_and_warnings without an alias rule.
The durable Dashboard/evidence path is a non-gap, but result and snapshot provenance is insufficient to reproduce or correlate failures.
The evidence lifecycle necessarily entails eviction/deletion, but deletion authority, atomicity, legal retention, user confirmation, and audit records are unspecified.
Empty dependency and ContractRef fields leave VerificationConfig, orchestrator, GateReport, Dashboard, registry, and EvidenceStore seams implicit.
Only migration/index validation surfaces are named; no behavioral oracle can falsify the runtime, GUI, failure, privacy, or evidence requirements.
The omnibus optional-feature unit, empty dependency graph, generic owner references, and non-behavioral validators prevent this window from bounding all downstream protocol and consumer gaps.
